title: FM Synthesis — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of FM Synthesis's rich face, its first round, a Sketch made in the proposal round of 2026-11: the staged patch gathered beside the doorway it begins from, and four made walks, each opening on one idea and ending on its section's claim, tested: the index at 1:1, the ratio families, the feedback loop to its edge, and the stack against the pair, with the three algorithm drawings the page asked for. I hold the fingerprint of the words each was laid against. I grow when Loudon has played the staged patch and the offers below are answered; I never hold the entry's words.

pieces.by: Web Audio Worklet · from the deposit of 2026-10-25 (4dc02656)
pieces.title: FM, in seven steps · the staged patch
pieces.caption: **The whole instrument as one walk.** One operator; a vibrato pushed past the threshold this paragraph opens on; ratio and index; the index given its own envelope; feedback; the other four operators and all 32 DX7 algorithms; a keyboard. Each step adds to the last without breaking it, and its checks re-run every step's claim. Gathered as it was built: the page's Forward Vector says it waits on Loudon's ears before it belongs here, so it stands as a proposal until he has played it.

verdicts.why: Its checks pass 32/32 and it walks one operator up to the DX7. The page says it waits on Loudon's ears before joining the face, so it stands only as a proposal: if the round lands unplayed, it comes out.

sections.heading: What the ear hears as the index rises

pieces.title: The index · brighter, or shimmering?
pieces.caption: **Held at 1 : 1, as the section holds it, and drawn twice: as FM makes the sidebands, and as they reach the ear.** It walks from a sine to the first pair, then the index-plus-one rule, then a slow sweep that tests the section's claim. The rule holds: the pairs carrying 98 % of the power never stray a whole pair from index + 1. The shimmer holds too, and goes further than the text says: at 1 : 1 even the brightness centre falls in places. One thing the text says doesn't hold at 1 : 1. The first pair's lower partner lands on 0 Hz and is silent, so you hear one new partial, an octave up, not one either side.

verdicts.why: A real test: the sweep's verdict could have read 'opening'. Its one disagreement with the text, the 0 Hz partner at 1:1, is flagged and recomputes exactly (−16.25 dB).

pieces.title: Ratios · on the grid, and off it
pieces.caption: **One pair, the ratio moved one step at a time against the note's harmonic grid.** It walks 1 : 1, 1 : 2, 1 : 3.5 (held against plain sines at 220 and 110), 1 : 1.414 and 1 : 1.003, then lets you set any ratio. The piece writes your ratio as two whole numbers and works out the shared fundamental and how often the patch repeats. The section's families all show up. So does what its scope line leaves out. 1.414 is itself 707 : 500, so the patch repeats, once every 2.27 s. The line the ear draws is a threshold, not whole numbers against the rest. The family names are the section's; the edges between them are this piece's rule, not yet checked by ear.

verdicts.why: Walks 1:1 to any ratio and lets the scope line fail in view. The caption owns that its threshold reading and family edges are its own rule, unheard. The piece reads 1:1.1 correctly; offer 4's wording of it does not.

pieces.title: Feedback · one operator, listening to itself
pieces.caption: **One operator in a loop, as Dexed models the DX7's.** It walks from a sine through the lean to 7, held against a true sawtooth, then past the edge, and ends on the section's claim across 0 to 10. Two meters run on the piece's own engine. At 7 the first ten harmonics sit within 1.0 dB of a sawtooth's and the wave repeats exactly. The loop holds to about 7.3, frays by 7.35 and is mostly noise by 7.4. Step 5 shows what the section takes for granted: the DX7 feeds back the average of the last two outputs. Without that average, the same push at 7 is already fraying.
pieces.near: A little feedback leans the sine

verdicts.why: Two meters on the engine test sine, lean, saw, fray, noise in order. The average and the edge near 7.3 also hold at 44.1 and 49.096 kHz and from 100 to 1600 Hz, which answers the maker's device-rate worry.

pieces.by: the Maker · TikZ, to the Technical Diagram Standard
pieces.title: Algorithms 1, 5 and 32
pieces.caption: The three wirings the section names, drawn from Dexed's routing rows. Those rows are checked against the staged patch's table of all 32. Algorithm 1 is a pair beside a stack of four; algorithm 5 is three pairs; algorithm 32 is six carriers. All three keep the one loop on operator 6. The TikZ source sits beside the drawing, and it is the truth; the SVG is its shadow.

pieces.title: Six operators · wirings of one pair
pieces.caption: **The DX7's own table, played and counted.** It walks one pair, a stack of three, algorithm 1, algorithm 5 and algorithm 32, and each one is drawn from its row with a count of its partials. The last step sets a stack against a pair you can push as hard as you like. At the same push the stack makes over twice the pair's partials (17 against 7). Off whole-number ratios no push lets a pair catch up (154 against at most 32). With whole numbers, though, a pair pushed to index 14 fills the same grid the stack fills at index 2. The counts are a floor: peaks closer than about 12 Hz count as one.
pieces.near: A stack is where it gets dense

verdicts.why: Illustrates rather than tests, but it is the drawing the Forward Vector asks for, and rendered it matches the routing rows and the DX7 panel. Taste note: the key's loop glyph looks like a plain wire.

The test caught the text's 'than a pair can' overreaching, and 7 vs 17 recomputes exactly. Caption fix: the stack at index 2 has 17 of 22 harmonics, so say the pair catches it near index 9 and fills all 22 by 14.

offers.section: What the ear hears as the index rises
offers.what: At 1:1 the first new partials are not heard as a pair. The lower sideband lands on 0 Hz and is silent, so a breath of index adds one partial, an octave up: −16.25 dB at index 0.3, where the engine and the Bessel maths agree to 0.01 dB. Suggested: "the first new partial has appeared, an octave up; its partner below the carrier lands on 0 Hz and is silent, since at 1:1 the spacing is the carrier itself." The index-plus-one rule holds as written: the pairs holding 98 % of the power stay within a pair of index + 1 from index 0.25 to 8, and index 4 gives five.

offers.section: What the ear hears as the index rises
offers.what: The shimmer goes further than the text says. At 1:1 even the overall brightness (the power-weighted mean frequency) falls as the index climbs in places: 483 → 417 Hz between index 2 and 3, and 925 → 807 Hz between 5.5 and 6.5. "It doesn't simply get brighter" could say so.

1.414 is itself a ratio of whole numbers, 707:500, so "the patch never repeats" is not strictly so. It repeats every 500 carrier cycles, once in 2.27 s at 220 Hz. Writing "1:√2 (about 1:1.414)" makes the sentence true as it stands.

To the ear, the scope line "whole numbers keep the series, anything else leaves it" is a threshold, not a line between kinds of number. Small whole numbers keep it: 1:3.5 is 2:7, a pitch at 110 Hz, and 1:1.25 is 4:5, at 55 Hz. Larger ones push the shared fundamental down until it is no longer a pitch. 1:1.1 is 10:11, a 22 Hz fundamental whose loud partials are its 10th, 12th and 21st harmonics. A hair off a whole number beats instead (1:1.01 at 4.4 Hz). That is the Duality's 20 Hz threshold again, which this page's own Forward Vector asks to measure. Suggested: "small whole numbers keep the series." The piece's family edges (a bottom number of 4, 20 Hz, 50 Hz) are its own, and no ear has checked them.

The text holds as written. This offers the reason, and where the edge is. The DX7, as Dexed models it, feeds back the average of the operator's last two outputs. With that average, 7 sits within 1.0 dB rms of a sawtooth over harmonics 2 to 10 and repeats exactly. A plain one-sample loop at the same push (π) is already fraying: 78 % of its energy repeats with the note, and it sits 8.3 dB from a sawtooth. Yamaha's top also sits just under the edge. The loop repeats exactly to about 7.3 (a push of 1.23π), frays by 7.35 (97 %) and is mostly noise by 7.4 (25 %). These numbers are for one 200 Hz note at 48 kHz.

"Route an operator's output back into its own input… each algorithm exactly one such loop" fits thirty of the 32. In algorithms 4 and 6 the one loop crosses operators: it runs from operator 4 (or 5) back to operator 6, round part of the stack. That reading comes from Dexed's rows, read through the staged patch's table. A clause would cover it: "in two of them the loop runs back across the stack instead."

"Pushing a carrier with a rich tone gives far more partials than a pair can" holds at the same push. A stack of three makes 17 partials and a pair 7, both at index 2, ratios 1:1:1. Once the ratios leave whole numbers it holds at any push: the stack makes 154 and the pair tops out at 32 by index 10. With whole-number ratios, though, a pair pushed to index 14 fills the same harmonic grid the stack fills at 2 (22 partials under 5 kHz). Suggested: "far more partials than a pair makes at the same push, and, off whole-number ratios, more than a pair can at any."

The three drawings the Forward Vector asks for are made: TikZ source and SVG in the bundle, with routing from Dexed's rows. Under Loudon's placement rule, a signal-flow diagram the text describes may belong in the text. The offer is to embed "FM Synthesis — rich — algorithms 1, 5 and 32.svg" after the paragraph that begins "An algorithm says three things", and to mark "Draw the algorithms" done. The drawing also shows that algorithm 32 keeps its loop on operator 6, so it is "six sines" only at feedback 0; a few words could say so.
